title: Region-pin validation middleware, RBACv2 shadow rollout, and audit canonicalizer
author: Ethan Voss
release_notes: Add region-pin enforcement middleware; introduce RBACv2 shadow decision path for gradual rollout; normalize audit-context headers to canonical format for downstream consumers.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight region-pin validation middleware at the API ingress, an RBACv2 'shadow' decision path (decision emitted to telemetry but not enforced) and an audit canonicalizer that normalizes audit headers and embeds KMS provenance assertions when available. The goal is to provide deterministic region pin checks for customer requests, incrementally validate RBACv2 policy decisions in production without disrupting traffic, and improve downstream audit consumers' ability to reason about request provenance and KMS region attributes.

Motivation and context: Customers in regulated geographies require consistent region pin enforcement and auditable traces linking KMS usage to enforcement decisions. We have rolled out RBACv2 policy authoring but need production validation of policy decisions before full enforcement to avoid regressions. We also have multiple audit header formats across services; the canonicalizer makes audits searchable and simplifies compliance reporting. This work ties together earlier Linear items ENG-3421 and SEC-118 and addresses support ticket SUP-9023.

What changed (high level):
- region_pin_middleware: new HTTP middleware placed in the API gateway and replicated in the private control-plane agent. Validates a request's claimed region against tenant configuration and service-bound region constraints. Emits reason codes and an enforcement decision.
- rbacv2_shadow: forked the PDP call path when shadow mode is enabled; decisions are logged to telemetry and the audit payload but are not used to allow/deny the request. Shadow decisions include policy fingerprint and trace id.
- audit_canonicalizer: component that normalizes incoming audit headers (X-Audit-Trace, X-KMS-Origin, X-Region-Claim) into a consistent JSON envelope and attaches KMS provenance tags when available. Implemented as a small lib used by gateway and audit-forwarder.
- KMS integration: audit canonicalizer queries the KMS usage metadata cache (read-only) to attach key region and provider fingerprint; it does not perform crypto ops.
- Tests & telemetry: unit tests for middleware logic, integration tests exercising region pin combos, and Telemetry added for shadow-vs-enforced decision delta.

Checklist:
- [x] Add middleware and unit tests
- [x] Add shadow PDP call path and telemetry emission
- [x] Normalize audit headers and add KMS metadata enrichment path
- [x] Add integration tests for multi-region tenant configs
- [x] Compatibility smoke test against existing audit-forwarder
- [x] Documentation: API gateway upgrade notes and binary flag docs for private installer

Design notes:
- Region pin rules are intentionally conservative: if tenant config absent, middleware prefers a permissive decision with a HIGH-PRIORITY telemetry marker so we can measure impact before strict enforcement.
- Shadow PDP is gated by a runtime flag (rbacv2.shadow_mode=true) scoped per-environment; decisions produce a single-line JSON blob to the audit log to minimize downstream parsing changes.
- Audit canonicalizer uses feature-detected headers (supports legacy X-Audit-* variants) and emits a canonical header X-Audit-Envelope containing base64(JSON) to avoid header size regressions.

Commits (summary):
- Add region-pin middleware and tests
- Implement RBACv2 shadow path and telemetry hooks
- Add audit canonicalizer library and link into gateway and forwarder
- Integration test: multi-region tenant matrix
- Docs: gateway upgrade notes and installer flag docs

Files changed (high-level):
- api/gateway/middleware/region_pin.go (new)
- api/gateway/middleware/region_pin_test.go (new)
- auth/pdp/shadow.go (new)
- auth/pdp/shadow_test.go (new)
- internal/audit/canonicalizer/* (new files: canonicalizer.go, formatter.go, canonicalizer_test.go)
- infra/installer/private_flags.md (docs)
- e2e/tests/region_pin_matrix.yaml (new test)
- telemetry/metrics/decision_delta.metric (tweak)
- pkg/kms/metadata_cache.go (read-only accessor)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Anya Patel: "Can the middleware be toggled per-namespace? For private installs we want a gradual opt-in."
  - Ethan: "Yes — middleware accepts a namespace whitelist from the tenant-store; for private installs we default to shadow for all namespaces and document the opt-in steps. Added notes in installer doc."
- Marcus Lee: "Two concerns: 1) header growth in audit forwarding, 2) potential duplication with forwarder enrichers."
  - Ethan: "Canonicalizer emits a single compact envelope header (base64 JSON) to avoid many small headers and replaced the forwarder's enrichment path with a call to the canonicalizer to prevent duplication. Forwarder now strips legacy headers after enrichment."
- Sofia Alvarez: "We should surface a short lived metric counting 'shadow denies' vs 'enforced denies' for policy owners."
  - Ethan: "Added telemetry/metrics/decision_delta.metric and tag shadow=true/false. Also added a dashboard query in the PR description for SRE (see below)."
- Marcus Lee (follow-up): "Unit tests look good but add a case where KMS metadata cache is stale/unavailable; canonicalizer should still emit a minimal envelope."
  - Ethan: "Added canonicalizer_test.go case and fallback behavior in metadata_cache.go; canonicalizer falls back to 'unknown' provenance fields and emits with provenance:unknown."

CI summary:
- unit: pass (all new unit tests + existing suite)
- integration: pass (region pin matrix tests)
- lint: pass with minor formatter warnings fixed in subsequent commit
- e2e: intermittent failure on existing audit-forwarder test on the first run; reran e2e and all green. Root cause tracked to test ordering; no code regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (now, merged): deploy binary with rbacv2.shadow_mode=true in production and middleware in permissive mode for tenants without explicit region pins. Shadow decisions will be captured for 2 weeks.
- Stage 2: after telemetry review, enable namespace-level opt-in enforcement for beta tenants (ops change).
- Stage 3: full enforcement with automated fallback on mismatch (policy: default-deny) once coverage and false-positive targets met.

Operational notes & runbook pointers:
- Telemetry dashboard (SRE): Metric decision_delta with tag shadow=true/false, filter by tenant and region, look for increase in shadow denies > 0.5% of traffic.
- Audit consumers: search X-Audit-Envelope for audit.trace_id and kms.provenance. If provenance is unknown, follow internal runbook SEC-RUN-09.

Backward compatibility and risks:
- The canonical envelope is backwards compatible: if consumers don't decode it, legacy headers are preserved for one release (forwarder strips them post canonicalization).
- Shadow mode is safe by design. The only risk is developer confusion with two decision streams; mitigated with dashboarding and documentation.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged by Anya Patel on 2026-02-05 after two approvals. CI green on final run.

Notes for auditors: The change set includes a focused set of logic touching gateway auth paths and the audit forwarder; all changes to KMS access are read-only metadata fetches and do not access key material. We added audit entries for both actual enforcement decisions and shadow decisions with a provenance tag to simplify compliance verification.
